Chapter 9. The Inner and Outer Purpose: Aligning with Life’s Flow.
As you become more present in your life, have you ever noticed those big questions about purpose start to bubble up? So many of us spend years searching for meaning—hoping the right job, the ideal relationship, or some big achievement will finally make us feel fulfilled.
But what if there’s a different way to look at it? The book offers a fresh perspective: it’s about seeing the difference between your inner and outer purpose.
Let’s start with outer purpose. That’s the one everyone talks about—the career you chase, your family roles, personal ambitions. And sure, those things matter, but here’s the catch: they’re always shifting. Jobs come and go, relationships change, life circumstances evolve. If your whole sense of self is wrapped up in these outer things, you might find yourself always striving, never quite feeling secure.
Now, inner purpose is something else entirely. It’s actually the same for all of us—to be fully present, to wake up to the reality of this moment, right here and now. This doesn’t mean you need to drop your goals or dreams. Instead, it’s about approaching everything you do from a place of true presence, instead of a sense of lack.
When you let inner purpose lead, your outer actions start to change. They become natural expressions of awareness, rather than desperate attempts to fill an emptiness.
Picture someone who’s spent years measuring success by achievements. Maybe they’ve ticked all the boxes and, on the surface, look successful. But deep down, there’s this emptiness—a sense that something’s missing. And in a quiet moment, the realization hits: what’s lacking isn’t another trophy, but a real connection to life itself.
When you bring your attention to the present moment—even during the most ordinary tasks—everything can shift. Work turns into an opportunity to serve, to create, to connect with others. Challenges aren’t just obstacles anymore; they become invitations to learn and grow. Suddenly, it feels like you’re being guided by something deeper than just personal ambition.
Now, aligning with life’s flow doesn’t mean giving up on your dreams or settling for less. Far from it. It’s about acting from a sense of wholeness—letting your actions come from a place of inner strength, rather than searching for fulfillment outside yourself.
And here’s something to really think about: most people don’t even realize how much energy they’re using up by resisting what is, or by chasing after what might be. But when you keep coming back to the present, again and again, a new sense of purpose starts to emerge. It’s rooted in presence, acceptance, and a quiet joy in simply being alive.
So, as you move through your day, maybe just pause and ask: am I aligned with life’s flow—right now?
